title: Pyrochlore Halves (working title)
idea: DICTO 2026-10-27: 'close packing halves rule pyrochlore network' — the rule of halves on the pyrochlore network, its layers stacked in any order.
construction: Close-packed stacking word (A,B,C), ball spacing 1, layers sqrt(2/3) apart. Diamond-type crystal = balls + #57's tetrahedral hole 'over X at 3/4' above each ball. Pyrochlore network = midpoints of its bonds: each atom's four bond midpoints a regular tetrahedron of edge 1/2; checked for 3C, 2H, 4H, 6H: every corner in exactly two tetrahedra. Per gap four sites: S (ball), C (diamond atom), O (octahedral hole), Y (tetrahedral hole over Y at 1/4); the two empty holes per gap are the network's voids.
weights: Power cells, w(S) = w(C) = lambda, w(O) = w(Y) = 0 (#57's census engine, exact rational arithmetic, unchanged).
walk_3C: Stops -3/8 (atom pieces vanish), -1/4 (atoms regular tetrahedra, holes truncated tetrahedra 12 corners: the tetrahedral-truncated tetrahedral (quarter cubic) honeycomb; truncated tetrahedron volume 23*sqrt2/96), +1/4 (roles swapped: atoms 12 corners, holes 4 corners), +3/8 (hole pieces vanish).
walk_2H: Stops -11/36, -1/4, -3/20, 0, 1/8, 1/6, 1/4 (exact). At -1/4 the diamond-atom pieces over hexagonal layers are regular tetrahedra but the ball pieces have 10 corners: the regular pyrochlore tetrahedra are exact pieces only on cubic layers.
rule_of_halves: O and Y pieces cut at the gap's mid-height into a bottom half (layer k) and top half (layer k+1); S whole (its own layer); C whole (nearest layer k+1). Every piece of 4H, 6H, 9R, 15R equals the same piece of the pure stacking of its layer (3C if c, 2H if h): 204 pieces at each of lambda = -1/4, -1/5, -1/10, 0, 1/10, none off (float, 7 decimals).
proof_status: PENDING: exact proof of the halves (as #57: locality over the 16 h/c windows of six layers, then exact corner functions per stretch). Exact walks for 3C and 2H done (census engine checks all PASS).
prior_art: Credited: the pyrochlore lattice as the bond-midpoint (medial) lattice of diamond and as alternating kagome and triangular layers along [111] (standard in frustrated-magnetism papers); diamond/lonsdaleite and zincblende/wurtzite stackings; the quarter cubic honeycomb (classical); the rule of halves (#57, DICTO). Not found in the sources searched (library of 302 references; web, 2026-10-27): the rule of halves for pyrochlore stackings or their weighted division.
